recentItems.title: Iran war latest: Dams, dirty bombs & doubtful sourcing | The Listening Post #shorts
recentItems.description:
A New York Times article linking Iran’s dams to its military, and a CNN report on an alleged Iranian dirty bomb plot, have drawn sharp criticism. 

Critics say both echo the wartime propaganda that accompanied the US’ war on Iraq: thin evidence, anonymous sources and well-timed claims. 

The Listening Post's Meenakshi Ravi looks at how reporting intelligence claims can at times end up amplifying and validating them.

recentItems.title: Deadline looms for Kataib Hezbollah to leave Jurf al-Nasr compound
recentItems.description:
A deadline is looming in a standoff between Iraq's prime minister and Kataib Hezbollah, one of the country's most powerful Iran-backed armed groups.

The group has been given until November 20 to leave its compound in Jurf al-Nasr, south of Baghdad, raising tensions over control of the area.

Al Jazeera's Peter Smith reports from Jurf al-Nasr.

recentItems.title: ICJ delivers landmark ruling in Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar
recentItems.description:
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) is delivering its judgment in a landmark genocide case brought by The Gambia against Myanmar over the military crackdown on the Rohingya in 2017.

The court has examined evidence of mass killings, forced displacement, sexual violence and other abuses against the Rohingya, with hundreds of thousands fleeing to Bangladesh. The central legal question is whether Myanmar's military acted with the specific intent to destroy the Rohingya, in whole or in part.

The ruling is being closely watched by Rohingya refugees seeking justice and by international legal experts, particularly because of its potential implications for other genocide cases before the court, including South Africa's case against Israel.

Al Jazeera's Steph Vassen reports from The Hague, while Tanvir Chowdhury speaks to Rohingya activists in Bangladesh.

recentItems.title: ‘Gaza Syndrome’: Israel’s soldiers haunted by genocide | Cost of War
recentItems.description:
What happens when Israeli soldiers return from Gaza?

The film Israel’s Soldiers Haunted by Genocide examines the psychological consequences of Israel’s genocide in Gaza through personal accounts of injury, grief and trauma by Israeli soldiers, alongside interviews with psychologists, journalists and Palestinian trauma specialists.

The film looks at the violence inflicted on Palestinians and asks how its consequences reach into Israeli families and society. Soldiers’ accounts of sleeplessness and fear sit alongside questions about military mental healthcare and the lasting effects of prolonged war.

Watch ‘Gaza Syndrome’: Israel’s Soldiers Haunted by Genocide, part of Cost of War, from Al Jazeera Originals.
